subject: English
passage: Augusta Savage's sculpture The Harp (1939) was the first major public artwork by a Black woman to be displayed at the New York World's Fair. The sculpture depicts a group of singing children whose bodies form the strings of a harp, representing the power of music in African American culture. The work reflects the ideals of the Harlem Renaissance (1918–1937), when Black artists sought to celebrate and elevate African American identity through art. The Harp thus shows how Savage used sculpture to honor the cultural contributions of Black Americans, which she continued to do throughout her artistic career.
prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To show how Savage's The Harp influenced other Black women to create public sculptures in the 1930s
choices.B: To give an example of how Savage celebrated the cultural heritage of Black Americans in her sculptures
choices.C: To illustrate how the themes Savage explored in her sculptures evolved over the course of her career
choices.D: To claim that several elements in The Harp were inspired by Savage's own childhood experiences

explanation: Choice B is the best answer. The text describes how The Harp depicted African American musical culture and the power of music in that community. It further states that Savage continued to use sculpture throughout her career to honor the cultural contributions of Black Americans.
